summary: The paper gives compiler techniques that generate SPMD message-passing code for rectangularly tiled, skewed iteration spaces. Tiles are assigned to processors first, data follow by the computer-owns rule, and communication is aggregated per tile.
why_read: It is an early, detailed treatment of compiling tiled loop nests for distributed memory, including local address translation and memory reduction.
main_contribution: A computation-first code generation scheme for tiled iteration spaces, with message-passing code for arbitrary and rectangular spaces and two memory optimizations.
main_limitation: The method needs rectangular tiling after skewing, and the evaluation covers a single stencil kernel on 1990s hardware.
evaluation_method: Measured speedup on a Fujitsu AP1000 for skewed SOR, with ablations of tile size, processor layout, validity-test cost and memory optimizations.
